### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fddb9cbb284830d40d2d663f9d1409f9b3b43c15`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fddb9cbb284830d40d2d663f9d1409f9b3b43c15` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `766b7c94ff5f0e3ab630ba54f0686a3b1033b6a2` — the merge of head `19243893f378eaa973cf0a5277915418b75452a0` into base `fddb9cbb284830d40d2d663f9d1409f9b3b43c15`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 766b7c94ff5f0e3ab630ba54f0686a3b1033b6a2 && git checkout 766b7c94ff5f0e3ab630ba54f0686a3b1033b6a2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin fddb9cbb284830d40d2d663f9d1409f9b3b43c15 19243893f378eaa973cf0a5277915418b75452a0 && git checkout -B drift-repro fddb9cbb284830d40d2d663f9d1409f9b3b43c15 && git merge --no-ff 19243893f378eaa973cf0a5277915418b75452a0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json fddb9cbb284830d40d2d663f9d1409f9b3b43c15
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs fddb9cbb284830d40d2d663f9d1409f9b3b43c15` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## L1 · PR #36084 · head `19243893f3` · **ACCEPT** (CI not concluded) · 2026-11-21T12:48Z

Card #35960. Claim 7062025264, report 7062798455. Clause-② no and Metadata-protocol none. There is no spec, governed or narrowing face, so this PR owes no L2. I read the whole diff against `8145424b53`, 10 files, +171/−55. That base already holds #36001 (`907b3783`), so the changeset's "for the share-grant subquery alike" is true at this head.

### What holds
- **One walk.** `primeOracleRawUuidColumns(object, where?)` seeds `{object}` and adds the objects returned by `collectTextMatchObjects(where, …)`. That is the same walker the SQL Server GUID prime uses: it adds `node.object` for each composed `ReadableIds` and recurses into its `scope`, so nested scopes are covered at any depth. It reads plain objects and arrays only.
- **Each target primed once.** Each target is primed once per object (`oracleRawUuidFieldsByObject.has(target)` → skip). Only federated objects are read. A failed catalog read records nothing, and the loop continues to the next target instead of returning, which is right: one parent's failure no longer skips its siblings.
- **List and leaf read the same map.** The leaf's `$in` arm from #36001 reads `oracleRawUuidFieldsByObject.get(table)`, where `table` is the scope's own object (`coercionKey` on the subquery's builder). The list's `coerceFilterValue` reads the same map, so both forms bind through `HEXTORAW` once the parent is primed.
- **Every Oracle door with a filter passes it.** That covers `findRows` (and with it `find` / `findOne`), `count`, `distinct`, `updateMany`, `deleteMany`, `analyzeQuery`, `findWithWindowFunctions`, and `aggregate`. `aggregate` passes `primedWhere`, so measure filters are folded in once and shared by the three primes; this is a refactor that changes no behaviour for SQL Server or PostgreSQL. Its joined parents pass `join.parent.scope`. The remaining Oracle-only call sites (`bulkCreate`, `findOne` by id, `sequence-semantics`) carry no `where` with a leaf, as I found on #35967.
- **Live pins.** Each door's first statement runs on a fresh driver, so nothing has read the parent yet. There are 2 forms × 10 cases:
  - find and its negation (`[c4]`, never every row);
  - count and the count of its negation;
  - distinct;
  - aggregate, in both `where` and a measure filter;
  - window functions;
  - analyzeQuery, whose SQL carries `HEXTORAW(`;
  - updateMany, which touches `[c1, c2]`;
  - deleteMany, which leaves `[c4]`.
- **Red/green.** 20 red on main, 20 green on the fix, and the ablation turns the same 20 red.
- **Changeset.** I checked it sentence by sentence. It also discloses the silent arm on main: no rows, and every row under negation.

### Nits (no re-review needed)
- **N1. Unpinned door.** The aggregate's joined parent passes its own composed scope, which is correct by reading, but no live pin covers it. On #35967 the joined-parent pin (`RelationGroupJoin` over a `character(4)` FK) was the template; an Oracle twin would close this here or in a follow-up.
- **N2. Claim surface.** `findWithWindowFunctions` fits the claim's clause ("the Oracle doors that call it with a filter in hand"), so I accept it. `sql-driver.ts`, however, is not named: its stub signature and docblock changed (+5/−3, line count steady). Post a one-line claim amendment record naming both.

### Owed
- **CI at `19243893f3`:** 12 success, 16 skipped and 22 in progress at the stamp, including Test Core 1–10, Build Core, every Type Check, and the lints (`query-options erasure` among them, after the two `as any` casts were removed). It is not concluded yet. This ACCEPT holds on this head once CI is green.
- **Oracle has no CI witness.** No CI job provisions Oracle, so the dev's local live runs are the only Oracle evidence for these 20 pins.
- **Out of scope:** window `orderBy` is not mapped through `columnMap` (ORA-00904). File it as its own card if it isn't one already.
